### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/cloud-connection`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **10** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **2** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `0bf4ae56423c6e2461becec9b33af063489d3f0d` — the merge of head `e30f9fc8a703d04c4952a0ecae3a7c90f1d56fc1` into base `8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 0bf4ae56423c6e2461becec9b33af063489d3f0d && git checkout 0bf4ae56423c6e2461becec9b33af063489d3f0d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90 e30f9fc8a703d04c4952a0ecae3a7c90f1d56fc1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90 && git merge --no-ff e30f9fc8a703d04c4952a0ecae3a7c90f1d56fc1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 8afaf12d7c302072871f7e975e9dff5be5541d90` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `e30f9fc8a703d04c4952a0ecae3a7c90f1d56fc1`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-artifact-lookup.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/index.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.lookup-artifact-item-call-sites.test.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts, packages/cloud-connection/src/marketplace-install-local-override-gate.test.ts, packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.test.ts, packages/qa/dogfood/test/email-template-override-unshipped-locale.dogfood.test.ts + packages/cli/src/utils/override-declarations.ts (the `os validate` walk, source unchanged), packages/metadata-core/src/item-key-discriminators.ts (`ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS`, `itemDiscriminator`), packages/objectql/src/registry.ts (`getArtifactItem`'s `member` narrowing), the verdict's call sites and `mergeArtifactProtection` in protocol.ts, skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md (the paragraph the follow-up names)

Face: narrowing — `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` · `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` on the PR body and on `.changeset/28746-override-gate-bundle-member.md`; `record-recognisers.mjs --paths` derives no schema or rules face from the ten changed paths (no `packages/spec/src/**`, no governed rule text), so the narrowing face is the whole of what is owed and its floor is every non-prose path of the diff. Reviewed against merge-base `5493b8842995fabb0979ae535301d3f3cb9fc65e` (origin/main at the dev's merge). Card #28746, triage#1, claim 6561473652, order-28746.md, os-dev-report 6562551938, epic #28236 N-09 and ADR-0146 D1/D2 read. PR author `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The identity comes from the registry's table, not a literal — correct.** `overrideWriteMemberOf(type, item)` is `itemDiscriminator(PLURAL_TO_SINGULAR[type] ?? type, item)` over `ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS` (`@objectstack/metadata-core`, the table the registry keys bundles on and `bundleMemberOf` reads for `mergeArtifactProtection`). At this head the table holds one key, `email_template: { field: 'locale', canonical: 'en-US' }` (item-key-discriminators.ts:68–70), so the dev's "only entry today" is measured true; a second bundle type added to the table is member-aware at every door with no edit here. A body naming no locale is the canonical member, which is how the read side and the save door's own `packagelessPairLanding` call (`itemDiscriminator`, protocol.ts:21168/22397) already read it.
2. **One spelling, four doors — holds.** `overrideWriteIdentityOf(type, identity, item)` = identity joined with the member by a NUL for a pair-identified type, identity unchanged otherwise. Its consumers: (a) `overrideWriteItemsOf` stamps `OverrideWriteItem.identity` through it (refusal.ts:528), which is what `os validate` / `os build` keys its `shipped` set and walked key on (`${type}\u0000${identity}`, override-declarations.ts:109–115 — source untouched, so the CLI door moved by composition alone) and what the install door's delivered packages carry; (b) the install door's `listedIdentity` (install-local-plugin.ts:586–593) returns it for an installed base's listed items — and that listing carries every member of a bundle with its `locale` (SchemaRegistry listing since #7730, slot-keyed merge since #7774, protocol.ts:3064–3078/10034–10044), so an installed base shipping `en-US` and `zh-CN` lists two identities, not one; (c) `overrideWriteVerdict` looks the registry up at the body's member and keeps only artifacts of that member. The save door (protocol.ts:21162, 22381, 22401), the per-item and package publish (:24001, judged on the draft body) and the flow-lock exception (:16911) all pass through `overrideWriteVerdict`, so the save door, `?member=` publish, package publish, `os validate`/`os build` and install-local compute `shippers` at one identity. No second spelling of the pair exists in the diff or in the three doors; no door was found that lacks the member, since every caller hands the gate the body.
3. **A declared override of an unshipped locale is refused `declared_package_ships_no_such_item` at each door — pinned.** The rule is `judgeOverrideWrite`'s existing branch (`!closure.shippers.includes(base)`), unchanged in order and code; only the sentence gains ` with locale 'fr-FR'` for a pair-identified type (the `ofMember` string is empty for every other type, so their sentences are byte-identical). Pinned at the save door and the `?member=fr-FR` publish on the real showcase (dogfood, `403 NOT_OVERRIDABLE`, no pair row, `fr-FR` 404), at `os validate` (CLI test, the one row) and at install-local (403, nothing registered, no ledger entry). No new refusal code, no second gate — the order's ruling held.
4. **A shipped-member override still passes — pinned at the canonical member; the non-canonical case rests on the registry's own pin.** All three files pin `en-US` declared → admitted. A base shipping a non-canonical locale (`zh-CN` only, or beside `en-US`) is answered by `getArtifactItem(type, name, pkg, member)`'s `entriesOfMember` narrowing (objectql registry.ts:6463–6479), pinned at `environment-overlay-email-locale-restart.test.ts:738` (`zh-CN` shipped member → the package's artifact); the verdict's `.filter(a => overrideWriteMemberOf(type, a) === member)` is a guard for a member-blind registry double, the same guard `mergeArtifactProtection` applies with `bundleMemberOf`. Correct; a non-canonical shipped-member control in this PR's own pins would have been tighter (observation, not a must-fix).
5. **The widening is real, correct under D2, and declared honestly.** On main `shippers` counted the NAME, so the pair's undeclared `fr-FR` beside a base `en-US` met `undeclared_same_name` and a sentence telling the author to declare an override of a member that does not exist. Under the ruled identity it collides with no base item: D2's declaration is the mechanism for *replacing an existing item*, and D2's undeclared-same-name refusal exists so that nothing is "served as a silent replacement" — the read side serves per member (`findServedOverlayRow`, the layered read, the list's slot-keyed merge), so a `fr-FR` the base never shipped replaces nothing. Admitting it is the order's "unaffected: an addition without `overrides`" ruling made true (it was the order's premise that was wrong, not its intent). The PR body and the changeset each carry an explicit **Widened** paragraph and the 维护者速读 says 另有一处放宽; the Acceptance notes name the falsified premise. Honest.
6. **The Clause-② line is right as spelled.** AGENTS.md step 3 admits `yes|no` plus *at most one arm* from the closed pair, `(narrowing)` being the BREAKING arm; a change that both narrows and widens cannot name both arms, and the `yes` already carries the surface additions (the widening, the new export). `yes (narrowing)` with the widening in prose is the only well-formed declaration of this diff; `check-changeset-no-major` reads `narrowed` beside a `(narrowing)` arm as consistent.
7. **Surface beyond the claim — each in scope and correct.** `protocol-artifact-lookup.ts`: an optional fourth `member` threaded to both `lookupArtifactItem` calls; omitted, byte-identical, and every other caller (`artifactLockLayerAt` :94 — a lock binds the NAME —, protocol-lock-version-gates.ts:445, protocol-packageless-overlay-migration.ts:301, protocol.ts:10533/11386) passes none. It is the only way the gate asks per member without a second lookup. `protocol.ts`: the private `shippedArtifactsOf` gains the optional parameter and forwards it; TypeScript emits a private member without its signature, so the published `.d.ts` does not move. `index.ts`: `overrideWriteIdentityOf` is a **new public export** of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`'s entry — correctly a `Clause-②: yes` item, and the changeset's last paragraph names it with its contract; `overrideWriteMemberOf` stays module-level (not in the entry), which is right, since cloud-connection needs the identity only. The call-site pin records the two sites' literal arguments with the reason — the pin's purpose, moved honestly.
8. **Unchanged set verified.** A declared override of a shipped locale admitted; an undeclared item at a shipped locale still `undeclared_same_name` (shippers at `en-US` contain the base); every non-bundle type's identity is its name (`overrideWriteMemberOf` is `undefined`, the NUL join never happens, the sentence is unchanged); the read side untouched.

### ② Semver level

`minor` on `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` and `@objectstack/cloud-connection` — the two packages whose published source the diff moves; `@objectstack/cli` moves tests only, so no entry is owed. The title carries `!`, the changeset the **BREAKING** banner, both declaration lines at line start, and one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. Consistent with AGENTS.md step 3 (a kind other than `none` ⇒ at least `minor` on a moved package; launch-window breaking ships `minor`) and with `check-changeset-no-major` (`narrowed` beside `(narrowing)`); the dev's sweep has `check-changeset-no-major.mjs --base origin/main` and `check-adr-0087-registration.mjs` exit 0, and CI `Check Changeset` is green on this head. **ADR-0087 disposition judged honest:** no key of any schema changes shape; a stored pair row declaring an override of an unshipped locale is (at rest) served as before under the base's `_packageId` with layered `code: null`; (at upgrade) nothing re-judges it at boot — if the base later ships that locale it becomes a real override; (next save) with `overrides` it meets the gate's own sentence naming the locale and the remedy, saved without `overrides` it becomes the pair's own member. Stated in the changeset's **At rest** paragraph and measured on the showcase; a migration would have nothing to convert.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev's open question (a dependent's template under the base's name at an unshipped locale is now admitted; keep?) — verdict: A, keep.** Under the ruled identity `(type, name, member)` the dependent's `fr-FR` replaces nothing the base ships, the read side already treats it as another item, and option B is exactly the second rule the order forbids ("one gate, no second gate"). Pinned in the CLI file (collides only at `en-US`). **One follow-up for the seat, p3, not a must-fix:** ADR-0146 D2 says a dependent "adds items under its own names", written at name grain before bundles were considered; what the base-named read (`?package=<base>&member=fr-FR` and the package-less read) serves when a dependent holds the only `fr-FR` of a base's name was not measured by this PR (its read side is unchanged and ruled unaffected). If it serves the dependent's body stamped with the base's `_packageId`, that is Context §5's silent-contribution shape at member grain and is the evidence D2 routes to #28390 option B; measure it and file, or record "coexists under its own `?package=`" and close.
- **Dev's out-of-scope note (a pre-gate mislabelled row is served under the base's `_packageId`, "dormant, not filed") — file it, p3.** "Dormant" assumes no deployment holds such a row; N-09's precondition census counted undeclared same-name rows, not declared overrides of unshipped members, so the count is unmeasured. The row's fate is correctly disposed in ② for upgrade; a card keeps the read-side oddity findable.
- **Skills-docs: correctly declared as `follow-up owed — skills/objectstack-platform/SKILL.md`.** SKILL.md:134 lists `email_template` among the honoured types and is silent on locale; nothing it teaches is falsified by this diff, so deferring is right and editing it here would have added a rules face. Per pm-dispatch SKILL.md:313 and review-checklist.md:18, **the seat files the owed card and rewrites `owed — FILES` to `#N` before ACCEPT** — the seat's step, not a dev must-fix.
- **Evidence.** Red-first at base `7a48bf73` reported per file (3/4, 2/2, 2/2) with the shipped-locale control green on base; ablation from committed `c5b07573` via `ablation-replace.mjs`, marker preflighted in dist, restored with `--absent` and a clean tree — the readings match the mechanism (dropping the member reds the refusals and the addition controls, nothing else). Two gaps, neither a must-fix: the CLI dependent pin was added after the ablation and its red-first is not reported (on main it reds by the same `undeclared_same_name` path as the pair addition); the shipped-member control is canonical only (①.4). Package suites, typecheck, the full dogfood battery under the lock (375 files / 3038 tests, exit 0) and the 69-family gate sweep (69 run, 0 unrun; three exit-3 prerequisites re-run green) are in the PR body and 28746-gates-ran.txt.
- **Overlap.** #28728 (install-local-plugin.ts, step 2e) is merged. Of the 31 open PRs, none touches `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts`, `override-declarations.ts`, `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` or `protocol-artifact-lookup.ts`; #28772, #28770, #28768 and #28731 touch `protocol.ts` at hunks nowhere near 17275, and #28770 touches `index.ts` at :249, not the :37 export line. No conflict.
- **CI at 2026-11-01T19:22Z:** no check red on this head; `Check Changeset`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`, `PR-body guards`, `Lint · PM dispatch-gates`, `Dogfood Regression Gate`, `Spec property liveness` green; the eight `Test Core` shards, `Build Core` and the `Type Check` / `Lint` jobs still in progress. Landing precondition ② (every check green) is the seat's to read before queueing; this record does not stand in for it.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing against the published spec on main: `OverrideDeclarationSchema` (ADR-0146 D2) grants a `<base>.custom` item the capability to *replace an item its base ships*; the bundle identity (`ITEM_KEY_DISCRIMINATORS`, mirrored from the spec and pinned against it by `registry-i18n-bundle-key.test.ts`) says an `email_template` item is `(name, locale)`. A declaration naming a locale the base never shipped is not a capability the spec grants — it declares a replacement of nothing — so this change takes nothing away from a consumer and makes the spec's own refusal (`declared_package_ships_no_such_item`) real at the grain the identity table already fixes for every read. Per file: `protocol-packaged-base-refusal.ts` holds against the code it cites (the registry lookup narrows by member, the read side's `bundleMemberOf` guard is mirrored, `judgeOverrideWrite`'s order is untouched); `marketplace-install-local-plugin.ts` holds against the listing semantics it relies on (every member listed, `locale` on each); the CLI walk holds unchanged by keying on `identity`; the dogfood test accepts the change on the real showcase doors against both arms and both controls. The SKILL.md paragraph is silent rather than wrong, and its follow-up is declared. ADR-0146 is not amended by this PR and needs no amendment for the narrowing arm; whether D2's "under its own names" should be restated at member grain is the ③ follow-up's question, not this diff's.
